title.en: Describing motion: velocity, acceleration and equations of motion
How fast, how far, how soon

text.en: A swimmer in a race, a car on a straight highway, a ball dropped from a tower: all move in a straight line. We describe such motion with a few numbers, and those numbers can predict where the object will be.

Motion along a straight line is called linear motion, the simplest kind of motion.
Speed is distance travelled per unit time. Velocity is displacement per unit time and also has a direction.
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity: a = (v - u)/t, where u is initial velocity, v final velocity and t the time.
For constant acceleration the first equation of motion is v = u + a t.
The second equation gives displacement: s = u t + 1/2 a t^2, and the third is v^2 = u^2 + 2 a s.
From the area of a trapezium under the velocity-time graph we also get s = (u + v)t / 2.
Graphs help: the slope of a distance-time graph is the speed and the slope of a velocity-time graph is the acceleration.
Motion in a plane, like a kicked ball or a satellite, needs two directions. Motion along a circle is called circular motion.

problem.en: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 2 m/s^2 for 5 s. Find its final velocity and distance.

prompt.en: State the three equations of motion and what each symbol means.

points.en: Velocity includes direction; acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
The equations of motion apply for constant acceleration.
Graph slopes give speed or acceleration.
Motion in a plane uses two directions.
